max: heads-up — after the runtime merge this morning we're seeing a KV-cache hit/drop regression on multi-GPU runs (tp=2, pp=4)

max: profiling shows overall token p99 latency up ~18% and kv-hit rate down ~25% compared to baseline build-1849

tasha: ouch. any obvious hotspot from the traces?

max: main things: all-reduce time increased, and the chosen GEMM kernel switched to a variant that appears to block longer on small sequence lengths. also noticed imbalance in per-device KV-shard size (some GPUs holding >1.6x keys)

perf-bot: perf-summary run=1854009876 baseline=1849001200
perf-bot: metrics: avg_latency_tokens=14.3ms->16.9ms (+18%), kv_hit_rate=0.75->0.56, allreduce_mean=0.9ms->1.6ms, batch_util=68%->54%

nora: could this be from the kernel-selector heuristics? we recently added sequence-length bucketing that prefers packed kernels for larger seq-lens — for short prefixes that might force less efficient paths

liam: also remember the batching heuristic change: we lowered max-batch-time to favor latency. that reduces batching efficiency and increases effective allreduce calls when TP/PP splits are uneven

tasha: concretely for KV sharding: with TP across shards and PP slicing, our current allocator does per-layer stripe assignment which can cause hotspots when KV cache is sliced by attention head mapping. if some PP stage holds more active prefixes it becomes heavier

max: attached a small snippet from the timeline (copied):

```
# timeline partial
device0: forward compute 1.9ms -> allreduce 1.7ms -> kv-merge 2.1ms
device1: forward compute 2.0ms -> wait allreduce 2.3ms -> kv-merge 0.7ms
device2: forward compute 1.8ms -> allreduce 1.9ms -> kv-merge 2.4ms
... imbalance visible, device1 waiting on allreduce longer
```

nora: hmm. two levers: 1) change KV shard assignment to be aware of PP stage token hotness (move to token-weighted round robin), 2) fallback kernel policy override for small-seq to ensure low-blocking kernels selected

liam: +3 — also try temporarily increasing max-batch-time back to previous to test batching efficiency impact. if p99 drops and allreduce frequency reduces, that confirms batching as amplifier

max: I ran a quick micro-experiment:
```
# experiment
config A: tp=2 pp=4 dp=1, kv-shard=stripe, kernel-policy=auto, max-batch-time=3ms -> kv_hit 0.56, p99 16.9ms
config B: tp=2 pp=4 dp=1, kv-shard=token-aware-rr, kernel-policy=force-smallseq, max-batch-time=6ms -> kv_hit 0.71, p99 13.5ms
```

tasha: that's promising — token-aware rr + kernel override gives most of the win. any tradeoffs on memory / tail latency?

max: memory slightly higher on device2 (~150MB) due to rebalanced shard placement but within headroom. tail latency improved too in that run.

nora: we should be careful about generalizing. token-aware RR needs fast telemetry of per-prefix activity — could add a cheap EWMA per-shard and rebalance on epoch boundaries (not per-request)

liam: also consider hybrid: keep DP-style replicate for top-k hot prefixes (very common in chat workloads) and shard the rest. replicating a tiny hot set reduces cross-GPU fetches and allreduce pressure

tasha: good idea. hybrid replicate-hot + shard-cold might be lowest friction to deploy. quantize the replicated chunk to int8 to reduce memory cost if needed

max: action items:
- nora to prototype token-aware-rr allocator (epoch EWMA) and add a cheap instrumentation metric (per-shard hotness) — try on canary nodes (ETA 2d)
- liam to run batching sensitivity matrix (max-batch-time 2/4/8ms) across tp/pp combinations and report allreduce frequency impact (ETA 1d)
- tasha to add a kernel-selector override knob for small-seq fast-path and run regression tests (ETA 1d)

perf-bot: task created #1234 kv-rebalance-proto assignee=nora priority=high

nora: I'll start the allocator proto today and push a bench harness that simulates skewed prefixes

liam: i'll schedule the batching sweep on the lab cluster after lunch

tasha: will open the kernel override PR and tag you for benchmark numbers

max: thanks all. let's reconvene after those runs — if hybrid replicate-hot proves stable we can roll as a graceful fallback in the runtime to keep tail latency predictable. :thumbsup:

nora: noted — will post the first proto logs in this thread when ready

liam: thanks — ping me if you need GPUs for the sweep

max: ending note — this feels like a kernel-selector + sharding + batching interaction, not a single bug. we should add an integration perf-test that exercises all three together to catch regressions early

tasha: agreed, i'll draft a checklist for CI perf gate items.
